journal_name: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a foundational theoretical framework that reconceptualizes representation learning in deep neural networks through the lens of information-theoretic principles. Unlike conventional approaches that optimize empirical risk, we establish a formal connection between the information bottleneck principle and the emergent representations in modern architectures, revealing fundamental constraints on feature compression and discrimination trade-offs. We prove that the popular training dynamics of gradient descent implicitly performs a variational approximation to the optimal information bottleneck solution, providing the first unified theoretical explanation for why deep networks learn hierarchical features. Furthermore, we introduce novel analytical bounds characterizing the representation complexity required for different pattern recognition tasks, which generalize classical VC-dimension analysis to deep learning settings. Our theoretical contributions yield practical insights: we derive new regularization terms that directly enforce optimal information bottlenecks during training. Extensive experiments on computer vision benchmarks validate our theory, demonstrating that networks trained with the proposed framework achieve superior generalization while learning more compact representations. This work fundamentally reshapes our understanding of representation learning by providing a mathematically rigorous alternative to prevailing empirical approaches in pattern analysis and machine learning.

We present a significant theoretical advancement in understanding and improving the generalization capabilities of deep neural networks through a novel PAC-Bayesian analysis framework. While existing PAC-Bayesian bounds provide theoretical guarantees, they often yield overly pessimistic estimates that fail to explain the empirical success of modern architectures. Our approach introduces a refined complexity measure that captures the data-dependent characteristics of learned representations, incorporating recent insights from deep learning practice such as the role of feature reuse and network architecture. We prove tighter generalization bounds that depend on the covariance structure of the network's internal representations, revealing why certain architectural design choices and training procedures lead to better generalization. The theoretical analysis yields an interpretable bound that can guide hyperparameter selection and architecture design. Based on these theoretical insights, we derive a novel regularization scheme that explicitly minimizes our bound during training. Experiments across multiple computer vision and pattern recognition benchmarks demonstrate that our approach consistently improves upon existing PAC-Bayesian methods, achieving better generalization with statistical guarantees while maintaining computational efficiency.

This paper introduces VisionTransformer-Medical (VT-Med), a novel end-to-end framework that fundamentally transforms medical image analysis by unifying global attention mechanisms with localized anatomical feature processing. Existing approaches typically treat medical images as natural scenes, failing to leverage domain-specific structural priors. Our framework introduces an Anatomically-Aware Attention module that explicitly incorporates prior knowledge about organ topology and tissue characteristics into the self-attention computation, enabling the model to reason about anatomical relationships across scales. The system incorporates a Multi-Scale Feature Integration pipeline that maintains both fine-grained tissue details and global anatomical context, addressing the critical challenge of detecting abnormalities at varying scales. We design a Task-Adaptive Head architecture that enables seamless multi-task learning across lesion segmentation, disease classification, and severity grading while sharing rich anatomical representations. Extensive validation on five challenging medical imaging datasets spanning radiology and pathology demonstrates that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods by substantial margins. The proposed system provides interpretable attention maps that highlight clinically relevant regions, facilitating physician trust and collaborative diagnosis in computer-assisted medical image analysis.

We present a comprehensive system design for real-time face recognition in unconstrained environments that substantially advances the state-of-the-art in both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed architecture, denoted as LightFace++, comprises three key innovations: (1) a novel Disentangled Identity-Preserving Representation module that explicitly separates identity-related features from ambient variations such as illumination, pose, and occlusion, enabling robust recognition across challenging conditions; (2) an efficient Progressive Feature Calibration network that hierarchically refines facial features with negligible computational overhead; (3) a dynamic Sample Reweighting strategy that adaptively emphasizes hard examples during training to address long-tailed distributions inherent in large-scale face datasets. Our system achieves 98.7% verification accuracy on the IJB-C benchmark, surpassing previous methods by 2.3% while reducing model parameters by 40%. The inference latency of 8ms per face on mobile devices enables practical deployment in real-time applications including video surveillance and mobile authentication. Extensive ablation studies and cross-dataset evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of each proposed component and the system's generalization capability for robust biometric recognition in production environments.
